title: Finite-level compact-support direct image commutes with restriction of scalars
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated morphism of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $c=(j,\bar f)$, $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, be a compactification of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]: $j$ an open immersion, $\bar f$ proper, $\bar f j=f$. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible on $Y$ (its image in $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is a unit), and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite commutative rings (for instance the reduction $A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$ for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an integer $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]). For $W\in\{X,\overline X,Y\}$ let $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] along the induced map of constant sheaves of rings $A_W\to B_W$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; it is exact, so applied termwise it defines a triangulated functor $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. Let $Rf^{c,A}_{!}=R\bar f^{A}_{*}\,j_!$ and $Rf^{c,B}_{!}=R\bar f^{B}_{*}\,j_!$ be the compact-support candidates attached to $c$ with coefficients $A$ and $B$, defined by these composite formulas, built from the extension by zero $j_!$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and the derived direct image defined with K-injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Then there is an isomorphism of functors $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$

$$
 Rf^{c,A}_{!}\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\circ Rf^{c,B}_{!},
$$

natural in the argument, namely the composite of the identification $j_!\operatorname{Res}_\varphi=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi j_!$ (both are computed termwise on the underlying sheaves of abelian groups) with the isomorphism $R\bar f^{A}_{*}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\cong\operatorname{Res}_\varphi R\bar f^{B}_{*}$ of [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars] for $\bar f$. For composable homomorphisms $A\to B\to C$ of finite commutative rings these isomorphisms compose to the one for $A\to C$.

external.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition) for the direct-image part, as in lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars
Section 6.1 (Lemma 6.1.11-6.1.13: $j_!$ on the pro-etale site, computed on underlying sheaves) and Definition 6.7.6 ($f_!=\bar f_*\circ j_!$)

proof.text: Write $p=\bar f$, $J_R=j_!^R$ and $r_{\varphi,W}=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi,W}$, suppressing $W$ when its scheme is forced by the expression. Restriction of scalars leaves the underlying abelian sheaf and each underlying morphism unchanged. Kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels, so their underlying abelian sheaves are unchanged by restriction; the induced actions on both are $a\cdot m=\varphi(a)m$. Thus $r_\varphi$ is additive and exact. By the exact-functor factorization theorem it carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and defines the stated triangulated functor on the unbounded derived categories, computed termwise. For $A\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\xrightarrow{\psi}C$, the actions on a $C$-module agree since $a\cdot m=\psi(\varphi(a))m$, and morphisms are unchanged. Hence $r_\varphi r_\psi=r_{\psi\varphi}$ on sheaves and termwise complexes, with the induced canonical identification on derived categories.

For a $B_X$-module sheaf $M$, use the presheaf $P_M$ in the definition of extension by zero. At $V\to\overline X$ factoring through $X$, both $P_{r_\varphi M}(V)$ and $r_\varphi P_M(V)$ are $M(V\to X)$ with $a\cdot m=\varphi(a)m$; otherwise both are zero. Their restriction maps and maps induced by $M\to M'$ agree. Their associated abelian sheaves are therefore identical. On that associated sheaf the $A$-action obtained by restricting its $B$-action extends the same action on $P_M$; uniqueness of the sheafified module action identifies the two $A$-module structures. This gives the canonical natural isomorphism $e_\varphi:J_A r_\varphi\xrightarrow{\sim}r_\varphi J_B$, induced by the identity of underlying presheaves and their sheafification units. For three coefficient rings, both the direct identification and the successive identifications are induced by the same presheaf identity, so uniqueness gives $e_{\psi\varphi,M}=r_\varphi(e_{\psi,M})\circ e_{\varphi,r_\psi M}$. The identification for an identity coefficient map is the identity.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), associated-presheaf formula, and Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), uniqueness of the action

proof.text: The exactness theorem for extension by zero applies to the given open immersion $j$ separately for each finite coefficient ring $A,B,C$. The exact-functor factorization theorem therefore realizes each $J_R$ termwise on unbounded complexes. Apply the isomorphisms of step 2 in every degree; their naturality makes them commute with the differentials. Both composite functors invert quasi-isomorphisms by exactness. The localization universal property, clause (2), descends these natural isomorphisms to the derived categories. Its preservation of composition and clause (3) descend the coefficient-composition identity of step 2 as well. Thus $e_\varphi$ and its composition law hold on all of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, with no boundedness or etale-origin restriction.

source.place: Tag 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); descent and equality of natural transformations by lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property

proof.text:
Apply the direct-image restriction-of-scalars theorem to the morphism $p:\overline X\to Y$ and the given finite rings. Write its natural isomorphism as $\beta_{\varphi,L}:Rp_*^A r_\varphi L\xrightarrow{\sim}r_\varphi Rp_*^B L$. For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ define
$$\alpha_{\varphi,K}=\beta_{\varphi,J_BK}\circ Rp_*^A(e_{\varphi,K}):Rp_*^A J_A r_\varphi K\xrightarrow{\sim}r_\varphi Rp_*^B J_BK.$$
This has the stated endpoints by the defining composite formulas for the two compact-support candidates. The two factors are natural isomorphisms, so their composite is a natural isomorphism and is exactly the comparison specified in the statement. The direct-image theorem applies to every scheme morphism; properness of $p$ is already part of the fixed compactification and needs no additional hypothesis for this application.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), via the existing normalized direct-image restriction-of-scalars theorem

proof.text: For composable coefficient maps $A\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\xrightarrow{\psi}C$ and $L\in D(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},C)$, choose a K-injective $C$-complex $H$ representing $L$, a K-injective resolution $u:r_\psi H\to I$ over $B$, and one $v:r_\varphi I\to T$ over $A$. The resolution-existence theorem applies on the small site specified by the pro-etale size convention. Exactness from step 1 makes $r_\varphi u$ a quasi-isomorphism, so $w=v\circ r_\varphi u:r_{\psi\varphi}H\to T$ is a K-injective resolution. Write $F_R=p_*^R$ on complexes, $Q_R$ for localization, and brackets for the localized maps.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); the existing resolution-existence theorem on small ringed sites

proof.text: Use the arbitrary-resolution morphism computation with the additive functors $F_A,F_B$ defining the direct images. For the map $r_\varphi[u]$, use source resolution $w$ and target resolution $v$; their common target is $T$ and $v\circ r_\varphi u=w$, so the unique comparison class is $1_T$. Consequently $Rp_*^A(r_\varphi[u])$ is the identity on $Q_AF_AT$ under these identifications. With source resolution $u$ and target resolution $1_I$, the same lemma gives that $Rp_*^B[u]$ is the identity on $Q_BF_BI$. The lemma's canonical transitions justify these computations for the chosen derived direct images, irrespective of their initially chosen functorial resolutions.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), expanded into the arbitrary-resolution computation lemma

proof.text: Apply the normalized-comparison common-resolution lemma with $\mathcal A'=\Sh(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, $\mathcal A=\Sh(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $\mathcal B'=\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, $\mathcal B=\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $r=r_\varphi$, $s=r_{\varphi,Y}$, $F=F_A$, $G=F_B$, $N=r_\psi H$, and the resolutions $u,v$ of step 5. These are abelian categories of module sheaves on the specified small sites; their K-injective resolutions exist. The functors $r,s$ are exact by step 1. The equality $F_A r_\varphi=r_\varphi F_B$ holds on complexes: on $V\to Y$, both sides evaluate on $\overline X\times_YV$ and restrict the action along $\varphi$. The direct-image theorem supplies the natural isomorphism $\beta_\varphi$ with precisely the required normalization. The lemma therefore identifies $\beta_{\varphi,r_\psi L}$ with $[F_Av]^{-1}:Q_AF_AT\to Q_Ar_\varphi F_BI$. It also supplies independence of the resolution identifications. This is the naturality calculation whose two vertical derived maps were computed in step 6.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); common-resolution naturality lemma, with the normalization from the existing direct-image theorem

proof.text:
For the K-injective $C$-complex $H$, the direct-image theorem identifies $\beta_{\psi,L}$ with $[F_Bu]^{-1}$ and $\beta_{\psi\varphi,L}$ with $[F_Aw]^{-1}$. All these maps are invertible by that theorem; no restriction functor is assumed to preserve K-injectives. Using step 7 and the equality $r_\varphi F_Bu=F_A(r_\varphi u)$ on sections gives
$$(r_\varphi\beta_{\psi,L})\circ\beta_{\varphi,r_\psi L}=[F_A(r_\varphi u)]^{-1}\circ[F_Av]^{-1}=[F_Aw]^{-1}=\beta_{\psi\varphi,L}.$$
This calculation is functorial in $L$ because the comparisons and canonical resolution identifications are natural. For an identity coefficient map choose the identity resolution of a K-injective representative; normalization gives the identity comparison.

Combine the two verified composition identities. Expand $\alpha_{\psi\varphi,K}$ by step 4, then use steps 3 and 8 to obtain
$$r_\varphi\beta_{\psi,J_CK}\circ\beta_{\varphi,r_\psi J_CK}\circ Rp_*^A(r_\varphi e_{\psi,K})\circ Rp_*^A(e_{\varphi,r_\psi K}).$$
Naturality of $\beta_\varphi$ for $e_{\psi,K}:J_Br_\psi K\to r_\psi J_CK$ identifies the middle two factors with
$$r_\varphi Rp_*^B(e_{\psi,K})\circ\beta_{\varphi,J_Br_\psi K}.$$
Substitution and associativity now make the whole composite exactly $r_\varphi(\alpha_{\psi,K})\circ\alpha_{\varphi,r_\psi K}$. This is the required coefficient-composition law under $r_\varphi r_\psi=r_{\psi\varphi}$. The identity cases checked above give the identity comparison as well.
